items.title: Albert Glenny Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: And I played with Charles Hippolyte. I played with a fine band. I played there. And they had two bands. Pierre Rose band and Hippolyte band.

ctx.x: Be right. Then the other part, then it's like a swing. You see the kind of word for that? Yeah. Yeah, that's my babe. That's one. That's one. All right. Now they got the other shots there, they get a slow drag. When he was coming, I get myself ready, but I didn't know you were surprised. Very young, baby. They all got time, eh? 20. I know. About stuff. 된 된 된 된 된 된 된 된 된 된 된 ! 된 된 된 된 된 된 된 ! 된 ! 된 된 stuff always slow. Yeah, that's right. That's right. There was a slow step then too? Yeah, you can make it, you can…

Oh, you mean, how old you mean? Well, I was a young man. I was about... Let me see. Don't ask me a little bit. Well, I was quite blind, you know. I knew how to play bass, but they had a bass player. You know? Were you about 20 years old at this time? 30? Well, I'll tell you. What was the bass? 27, 28, so. 27, 28. Yes. Was it before the Spanish-American War or after? At the same time, that was the time I'm talking about, especially during the war. During the war? I ain't been so long. That's right. That band…
I know. I haven't heard of it yet. They've all told us about you. We know that. We've heard about it. I'm not joking. I know.
